title: FAA DRPDS architecture questions to synthetic diagnostic-core coverage

semantics.purpose: Records which architecture questions are represented, partially represented, or not represented by the current synthetic core fixture.

coverage_levels.partial: A synthetic mode exercises a related endpoint or simplified fault shape, but does not cover the full evidence requirements or distinguish all hypotheses in the architecture question.
coverage_levels.none: The synthetic fixture has no defensible analogue for this architecture question.

mappings.rationale: The synthetic fixture has no utility-source identity, upstream origin, shared-supply dependency, or site-documentation evidence. Separate virtual source-evidence channels do not establish physical independence.

The two virtual source-evidence channels provide only partial source-boundary signal test-shape correspondence; source-side independent confirmation, sensing-fuse discrimination, utility-source independence, and physical source condition are not modeled.

constraints: A partial mapping is test-shape correspondence only; it is not evidence that the synthetic mode diagnoses the architecture question.
No architecture question is converted into a MeasurementRequest by this crosswalk.
Synthetic fixture points and values remain software-only and must not be mapped to physical FAA terminals or measurements.
Unmapped questions are explicit coverage gaps, not healthy states or negative diagnoses.
New source, generator-bus, SWGR-section, and standby-transfer modes are isolated virtual evidence-channel patterns; they do not encode source-to-section wiring or a transfer sequence.
The control-power prerequisite is architecture-level only; the synthetic fixture does not model AC/DC auxiliary power or battery behavior.
Load-bank test-path coverage is absent from the synthetic fixture; no load-bank operation or switching sequence is represented.
Transformer input/output and protection diagnostics are architecture-only; the synthetic fixture has no transformer fault or sensing-fuse discrimination modes.
